naturalness.finding: Social fabric is a conventional figurative noun for relationships/structures connecting a society or community. Strengthen the social fabric is a natural compositional predicate+noun use; source does not itself establish an earlier rupture or threatened collapse.

primaryReferences.title: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: fabric, figurative social structure sense
BBC Learning English: social fabric as community relationships

ownerComparisons.title: knit the social fabric back together
ownerComparisons.taughtDecision: Restore relationships after a prior rupture; back together requires an earlier connected state and observed reconnection.
ownerComparisons.whyNotSameSenseOwner: The volunteer sentence says strengthen; it gives neither a previous rupture nor restoration. Adding bare social fabric would make this repair lesson accept improvement cases its Step 3 deliberately rejects.

ownerComparisons.title: keeps the social fabric from coming apart
ownerComparisons.targetPattern: \bkeep(?:s|ing)? the social fabric from coming apart\b|\bkept the social fabric from coming apart\b
ownerComparisons.taughtDecision: Maintain existing ties despite pressure and prevent them from coming apart.
ownerComparisons.whyNotSameSenseOwner: Strengthening may create or deepen ties without a stated risk of coming apart. Adding the noun alone would erase the maintenance-versus-improvement distinction in the brief and assessed scene.
